records.name: Perth Art Gallery
records.description: Perth Art Gallery is the principal art gallery and exhibition space in the city of Perth, Scotland. It is located partly in the Marshall Monument, named in memory of Thomas Hay Marshall, a former provost of Perth.

records.name: St Ninian's Cathedral
records.description: St Ninian's Cathedral in Perth is a cathedral of the Scottish Episcopal Church in the Diocese of St Andrews, Dunkeld and Dunblane.

records.name: Fair Maid's House
records.description: Fair Maid's House is an historic building in the centre of Perth, Perth and Kinross, Scotland. Located in North Port, it is a Category B listed building, partly dating from 1475 but mostly from 1629.

records.name: Balhousie Castle
records.description: Balhousie Castle, located in Perth, Scotland (on Hay Street, originally a few hundred metres north of the medieval town), was built in the 17th century.

records.name: Branklyn Garden
records.description: Branklyn Garden is a hillside public garden in the Kinnoull area of the Scottish city of Perth. The garden is set in 2 acres (0.81 ha) in the western foothills of Kinnoull Hill.

records.name: Kinnoull Hill Woodland Park
records.description: A scenic outdoor stop around Perth, suited to walking, views, and a slower look at Perthshire.
records.address: Kinnoull Hill Woodland Park, Perth, Scotland

records.name: Kinnoull Tower
records.description: A rewarding viewpoint near Perth with broad scenery over the surrounding landscape of Perthshire.

records.name: North Inch
records.description: A scenic outdoor stop around Perth, suited to walking, views, and a slower look at Perthshire.

records.name: South Inch
records.description: South Inch is a large public park in Perth, Scotland. About 31 hectares (77 acres) in size, it is one of two "Inches" in Perth, the other being the larger, 57-hectare (140-acre) North Inch, located half a mile across the city.

records.name: Perth Bridge
records.description: Perth Bridge (also known as Smeaton's Bridge, locally, the Old Bridge, and in the local dialect of Scots, the Auld Brig) is a toll-free bridge in the city of Perth, Scotland. A Category A listed structure, it spans the River Tay, connecting Perth, on the western side of the river, to Bridgend, on its eastern side, carrying both automotive and pedestrian traffic of West Bridge Street (the A85).

records.name: Rodney Gardens
records.description: Rodney Gardens is an urban garden in the Kinnoull area of the Scottish city of Perth, on the eastern banks of the River Tay. Named for Admiral George Rodney of the Royal Navy, the gardens are situated on the former site of a mill.

records.name: Huntingtower Castle
records.description: A historic castle tied to the wider heritage of Perth and a strong stop for exploring Perthshire.

records.name: Elcho Castle
records.description: A historic castle tied to the wider heritage of Perth and a strong stop for exploring Perthshire.

records.name: Cherrybank Garden
records.description: A landscaped garden or estate stop near Perth, valued for seasonal colour and heritage setting.

records.name: Perth Racecourse
records.description: Perth Racecourse is a thoroughbred horse racing venue adjacent to the ancient Scone Palace, near Perth, Scotland. Perth Racecourse at the site in Scone Palace Parklands opened in 1908, just south of the ancient Cramock Burn, and is the northernmost track in Britain.

records.name: The Fergusson Gallery
records.description: A cultural stop in the Perth area showcasing art, exhibitions, or local creative history.

records.name: Moncreiffe Hill
records.description: A rewarding viewpoint near Perth with broad scenery over the surrounding landscape of Perthshire.

records.name: Moncreiffe Island
records.description: A scenic outdoor stop around Perth, suited to walking, views, and a slower look at Perthshire.

records.name: Norie-Miller Walk
records.description: Norie-Miller Walk is an urban park in the Scottish city of Perth, on the eastern banks of the River Tay. Named for Sir Stanley Norie-Miller, Bt, MC, DL, JP (1888–1973) it is situated between Smeaton's Bridge to the north and Queen's Bridge immediately to the south, and behind Kinnoull Parish Church.

records.name: Perth City Hall
records.description: Perth City Hall is a notable historic building in or near Perth, reflecting the area's civic and architectural story.

records.name: St John's Place
records.description: A historic quarter or settlement area that helps define the character of Perth.

records.name: Quarrymill Woodland Park
records.description: A scenic outdoor stop around Perth, suited to walking, views, and a slower look at Perthshire.

records.name: Stanley Mills
records.description: The Stanley Mills woollen mill at Ryeford, near Stonehouse, Gloucestershire, England was built in the early 19th century. The main building is Grade I listed.

records.name: Scone Palace
records.description: Scone Palace is a Category A-listed historic house near the village of Scone and the city of Perth, Scotland. Ancestral seat of Earls of Mansfield, built in red sandstone with a castellated roof, it is an example of the Gothic Revival style in Scotland.

records.name: Moot Hill
records.description: Scone Abbey (originally Scone Priory) was a house of Augustinian canons located in Scone, Perthshire (Gowrie), Scotland. Dates given for the establishment of Scone Priory have ranged from 1114 A.D.

records.name: Kinfauns Castle
records.description: Kinfauns Castle is a 19th-century castle in the Scottish village of Kinfauns, Perth and Kinross. It is in the Castellated Gothic style, with a slight asymmetry typical of Scottish Georgian.

records.name: A K Bell Library
records.description: A K Bell Library is a notable historic building in or near Perth, reflecting the area's civic and architectural story.
records.address: A K Bell Library, Perth, Scotland

records.name: St Paul's Church
records.description: A historic church connected with the religious heritage of Perth and the surrounding district.

records.name: Perth Harbour
records.description: Perth Harbour is a notable landmark around Perth that helps shape local itineraries through Perthshire.

records.name: Deuchny Wood
records.description: A wooded extension of the Kinnoull Hill walks, Deuchny Wood leads to clifftop paths and panoramic viewpoints over Perth, the River Tay, and the wider valley.

records.name: Perth Sheriff Court
records.description: Perth Sheriff Court is a substantial civic landmark in the city centre, representing the Victorian legal and administrative history of Perth.

records.name: Caithness Glass Visitor Centre
records.description: Linked with Perth's glassmaking heritage, the Caithness Glass visitor centre and factory-tour experience highlights the craftsmanship behind the company's famous art glass and paperweights.

records.name: North Inch Golf Course
records.description: Set beside one of Perth's great riverside parks, North Inch Golf Course adds a historic sporting layer to the open green space along the Tay.

records.name: North Inch Park Loop
records.description: The loop paths around the North Inch offer an easy way to enjoy mature trees, open grassland, and long river views close to central Perth.

records.name: St Leonard's-in-the-Fields Church
records.description: Overlooking the South Inch, St Leonard's-in-the-Fields is a striking Gothic Revival church built in the 1880s and one of Perth's finest listed ecclesiastical buildings.
